Two bugs, both in recency bookkeeping in `lrucache/cache.py`:

- `get` never called `move_to_end`, so reads didn't refresh recency and recently-used entries got evicted too early (`lrucache/cache.py:31`).
- `put` evicted the LRU entry before checking whether the key already existed, so updating an existing key in a full cache wrongly evicted a different entry (`lrucache/cache.py:34`).

Fixes are one line each; `SOLUTION.md` written as requested. No test files touched, no commits made.

- `put` evicted the LRU entry even when the key already existed — the capacity check now only runs when inserting a new key (cache.py:35), so updating an existing key in a full cache no longer evicts an unrelated entry.

`SOLUTION.md` written with the root-cause explanation.

Findings written to `findings.md`. Six defects introduced by the diff:

- `src/sync.py:14` — pagination off-by-one: `total_count // PAGE_SIZE` drops the last partial page (and all rows when the count is under one page).
- `src/sync.py:24` — mutable default `seen=[]` persists across calls, so future syncs skip previously processed users.
- `src/sync.py:31` — IDs are marked as seen before the UPDATE succeeds, so failed users are never retried.
- `src/sync.py:35` — f-string SQL interpolation of `email`/`id`: SQL injection plus breakage on quotes.
- `src/report.py:7` — early return on empty `users` leaks the open file handle.
- `src/report.py:11` — `email.lower().split("@")[1]` crashes on `None` emails (explicitly nullable per `db.py`) and on addresses lacking `@`; the old code handled `None` with a fallback.

I deliberately did not flag the `except Exception: pass` log removal or the missing `ORDER BY` in pagination, as those are behavior/style concerns rather than clear-cut defects on their own.

I reviewed the diff against the post-change files and wrote 8 findings to `findings.md`:

**`src/sync.py`**
- **Line 14** — off-by-one in pagination: `total_count // PAGE_SIZE` drops the final partial page (and everything when `total_count < 100`), so staged users are silently never fetched.
- **Line 17** — `LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` without `ORDER BY` makes page boundaries nondeterministic; rows can be skipped or duplicated across pages.
